title: A pressure-by-volume term gave no clear six-month ENSO forecast gain at 2000-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether pressure changes the forecast value of equatorial Pacific warm water volume in a simple ENSO model. The reference used seasonal surface temperature history, basin volume and a trailing three-month Southern Oscillation Index. The test added pressure times volume with annual harmonics. Fits used only eligible earlier targets. Across 300 monthly origins in 2000-2024, six-month mean squared error fell by 1.08%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -3.23% to +4.27%. Root mean squared error changed from 0.65749 C to 0.65393 C. Shorter training and curved surface temperature controls reversed the point gain. All six planned three-year-block comparisons had intervals that include zero. One secondary nine-month five-year-block interval favored the reference. These data give no clear added forecast value for the tested product terms. They do not exclude physical state-dependent coupling. Revised sources, one ocean analysis, model form, 25 test years and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The package has code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, numerical audits and a figure. Raw and monthly source-derived records remain external.
